concepts.label: Tombstone (Sync Gateway)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the mobile-notification-purpose artifact ('the means by which mobile clients are notified that a document has been deleted'), structurally a bare document revision (doc id + rev id + deleted:true). Kept as its own concept rather than folding directly into the promoted storage:tombstone: this page states the two BECOME the same on-disk object under one specific configuration (shared bucket access), which is a stated identity in one direction, not an unconditional identity - see the isVariantOf relation below.

concepts.label: Channel Cache (Sync Gateway, in-memory)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - Sync Gateway's in-memory per-channel cache, distinct from the revision cache described in revisions.md; new in this batch, recurs heavily in the stats-monitoring pages later in this same batch (chan_cache_* stats) where it will be reused as extraction-layer

concepts.label: Metadata Purge Interval (tombstone purge interval, Couchbase Server)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted in server/8.0/manage/manage-settings/configure-compact-settings.json extraction; this page is the first to state that a MOBILE deployment's tuning of this Server-side setting is governed by mobile client replication frequency rather than by Server-side storage concerns alone

relations.subject: sgw:tombstone
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted) - subject minted, object reused (promoted). A genuine explicit-statement case, unlike the sgcollect_info/cbcollect_info near-miss elsewhere in this batch: the page directly states the two become the same object under a stated condition, licensing the relation rather than a silent separate minting.
relations.evidence: When mobile tombstones sync with a Couchbase Server (that is, when `enable_shared_bucket_access: true`) they become server tombstones. The document body is deleted, and only the mobile sync metadata required to replicate the tombstone is retained in the mobile extended attribute.

relations.subject: sgw:tombstone
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted) - subject minted, object reused extraction-layer
relations.evidence: The server's `metadata purge interval` becomes an important consideration for sync'd mobile deployments. Because, when the server purges a tombstone (based on the `metadata purge interval`), that tombstone is no longer replicated to mobile clients.

relations.subject: storage:metadata-purge-interval
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted) - subject reused extraction-layer, object minted; distinct from the requiresSetting relation above by direction - this states the causal effect of the purge running, that one states the dependency
relations.evidence: The default `metadata purge interval` is set to 3 days which can potentially result in tombstones being purged before all clients have had a chance to be notified.

relations.subject: sgw:tombstone
relations.evidence: Running the [/{db}/\_compact](../rest-api/rest%5Fapi%5Fadmin.md#tag/Database-Management/operation/post%5Fdb-%5Fcompact) endpoint will remove purged tombstones from the channel cache

relations.subject: sgw:channel-cache
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted) - both minted; the explicit negation that motivates the whole 'Cache Ejection' section - restarting/compacting is required precisely because the cache does NOT self-clean
relations.evidence: Deleted/expired tombstones aren't automatically ejected from Sync Gateway's in-memory channel caches.

notable_absence.finding: No failure-then-cleanup shape on this page - purging and cache ejection are both routine maintenance operations described with no failure mode at all, unlike round 26's Server node-recovery operations which explicitly described what to do when a step fails.

cross_component_finding: This page cites Couchbase Server's own bucket-settings pages (Auto Compaction with UI, Creating and Editing Buckets) for HOW to tune metadata purge interval, but frames WHY entirely in mobile-replication terms - 'set the server's metadata purge interval based on their expected client replication frequency, to ensure that clients are notified of the tombstone prior to that tombstone being purged.' This is a genuinely new piece of cross-product tuning guidance that neither the Server storage docs nor round 3's SG access-control docs state: a Server-side setting's correct value depends on a Sync-Gateway-side deployment fact (client replication frequency), which only this manage/ page connects.
cross_product_finding: The isVariantOf relation above (sgw:tombstone isVariantOf storage:tombstone) is the strongest same-shape-different-product finding in this batch, and it goes the OPPOSITE direction from the sgcollect_info/cbcollect_info near-miss: there, two products' same-shaped tools are kept separate because no page states a relationship; here, the page explicitly states the objects literally become one another under a named condition (enable_shared_bucket_access), licensing the merge-adjacent relation rather than a silent separate minting. Table 1 and Table 2 on this page describe, cell by cell, exactly how the SAME logical delete operation produces different physical artifacts (document-body-retained vs xattr-only) depending on which product performed the delete (Sync Gateway vs Couchbase Server) and which access mode is configured - a level of cross-product mechanical detail with no precedent in round 3's access-control extraction, which never touched the storage layer at all.
